clue.text: You risk beggary, living in mine

definitions.text: You risk beggary, living in mine

parts.words: You risk beggary, living in mine
parts.note: the setter warns that anyone living close by them will be pestered to lend things, the area round their own home

explanation.surface: A grim warning that settling in the speaker's mining district will leave you a pauper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like a coal mine; it is the possessive, the area where I live, and the borrowing habits of the people next door are the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The district round one's home is the area where the people living close by are found.

clue.text: Northern Queensland, place for hire purchase ?

definitions.meaning: the remote outback of northern Australia has this nickname
the never-never is British slang for buying on instalments, so its land is where such buying happens

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a region of Australia is where things are bought on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Australians name the remote outback this; Peter Pan's fantasy island has the same name, and the never-never is British slang for instalment buying.

clue.text: Photograph included of fashionable group

parts.note: in means fashionable
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A snapshot taken of a trendy crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A small picture placed within a larger page or map is a picture set into it.

clue.text: Self-willed as Mrs Malaprop's allegory

definitions.meaning: stubbornly determined to have one's own way
in Sheridan's The Rivals Mrs Malaprop says a girl is as stubborn as an allegory on the banks of the Nile, meaning an alligator

explanation.surface: Someone is as stubborn as the comic character's garbled comparison.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Malaprop, in Sheridan's play The Rivals, misuses words; her famous line compares a stubborn girl to an 'allegory' on the Nile.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinate and determined to have one's own way is how Mrs Malaprop described her niece.

clue.text: Iridescent materials forming on a pile

indicators.note: letters materialising into a new shape signals that they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Shimmering fabrics heaped up in a stack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'materials' looks like part of the definition, but 'materials forming' tells us ON A PILE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Like an opal, showing shifting milky colours in the light.

clue.text: Make a come-back like Apollo

definitions.meaning: the Apollo spacecraft came back into the atmosphere from the Moon

explanation.surface: A performer stages a return as triumphant as the sun god's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apollo' suggests the Greek god; it is the American moon programme whose capsules came back into Earth's atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: To return into a place, as a capsule returning through the atmosphere does.

clue.text: Worthless river?

definitions.meaning: read as O plus a word for value or benefit, that is nothing of any utility
a river of Yorkshire, and another in East Anglia

explanation.surface: A dismissive question about a useless stretch of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worthless' is read as 'zero use', O followed by a four-letter word for utility, giving the name of an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: England has several rivers of this name, including the one through York; read as zero plus utility it means having no worth.

clue.text: Feeding expert tells artist to drop dead

parts.note: to drop dead is to die
Titian was the great Venetian painter

explanation.surface: A nutritionist rudely rebuffs a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tells' and 'to' are link words; the order of the pieces is DIE then TITIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist in diet and nutrition advises on what people should eat.

clue.text: But it is of importance to astronauts

definitions.text: But it is of importance to astronauts

parts.words: But it is of importance to astronauts
parts.note: a paradox: importance is weight, yet what matters to people in orbit is the absence of weight

explanation.surface: A rejoinder that something trivial still matters to space travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: In orbit astronauts float because they experience no apparent weight.

clue.text: Subjection of a Las Vegas eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of the words before it are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A satirical remark that Las Vegas is in thrall to something odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' reads as describing Las Vegas, but it signals that A LAS VEGAS is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Feudal servitude to a lord was the state of subjection a serf or retainer lived in.

clue.text: Nameless events — back the old Derby winner

indicators.note: back asks for the shortened word to be read from its last letter to its first
Nameless tells us to drop the abbreviation N, for name, from the word that follows

explanation.surface: A racing note about past contests whose winner is now forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nameless' drops N from EVENTS to leave EVETS, and 'back' turns that round. Steve Donoghue was a famous jockey who rode six Derby winners in the 1920s; the Derby is England's great flat race at Epsom.
explanation.definitionFit: Steve Donoghue, the jockey, was a celebrated Derby-winning rider of the past.

clue.text: Ceremonies we should stand up for, you say?

indicators.note: you say signals that the letters entered are said exactly like the word the clue phrase gives

parts.note: the entitlements we should defend are our rights

explanation.surface: A question about which rituals deserve our respect by rising to our feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand up for' suggests rising during a ritual, but it means defend: we stand up for our rights, which sound the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal religious or solemn rituals are observances of this kind.

clue.text: The letter I received from Greece

definitions.text: The letter I received from Greece

parts.words: The letter I received from Greece
parts.note: read not as a message that came by post from Greece but as the Greek alphabet's own version of the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone mentions a letter that arrived in the post from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Greek alphabet the ninth character corresponds to our I, and it also means a tiny amount.

clue.text: Call made by Alberich

definitions.meaning: to call someone on the telephone
in Wagner's operas the dwarf Alberich forges the magic band of the Nibelung from the Rhinegold

explanation.surface: A remark about a shout uttered by the Wagnerian dwarf.
explanation.definitionFit: To telephone is to give someone a buzz; Alberich forged the circlet at the heart of Wagner's cycle of four operas.

clue.text: Bold soldier Ben's joint at sea

parts.note: Thomas Hood's comic poem begins 'Ben Battle was a soldier bold', so this is Battle's
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: A wounded veteran's hip is troubling him on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Battle is the hero of Thomas Hood's comic ballad 'Faithful Nelly Gray', who loses his legs in war; 'at sea' is a loose definition, a warship being found there.
explanation.definitionFit: A large heavily armed warship is the kind of vessel found at sea.

clue.text: Express approval of a band of heralds

definitions.meaning: to back or sanction something publicly
in heraldry this is a narrow vertical stripe on a shield, a smaller form of the pale

explanation.surface: Applauding a troop of trumpeting messengers.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a candidate or product is to sanction it; heraldic designers use the term for a slim upright strip.

clue.text: Devilish flavour — how I loathe it!

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, so devilish suggests his name
relish is flavour or zest

explanation.surface: A diner grimaces at a fiendish taste.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis is the classical ruler of the underworld, a stand-in for the Devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste or dislike is the feeling expressed by an exclamation of loathing.

clue.text: Prophet's son-in-law, among others, was no dreamer

indicators.note: among puts the name of the son-in-law inside the word for the others

parts.note: the others means the rest
Ali married Fatima, daughter of the Prophet Muhammad

explanation.surface: A historical remark that a religious figure's relative was, like his peers, practical-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was' is a link; the definition is 'no dreamer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical person who faces facts as they are is the opposite of a dreamer.

clue.text: Sadly sees one's lost love joined this sect

indicators.note: sadly means badly or wretchedly, telling us to put the letters into a new order
lost says a letter goes missing from the word before it

parts.note: taken as its letters without the apostrophe
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A heartbroken person who has lost a partner turns to a religious community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes O ('love', zero in tennis) from ONE'S to leave NES; 'Sadly' scrambles SEES + NES. The Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect at the time of Christ.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an ascetic Jewish religious group of the Second Temple period.

clue.text: The sign of Rehoboam's scourge

definitions.meaning: in the Bible King Rehoboam threatened to chastise his people with scorpions rather than whips

explanation.surface: A biblical king's whip turns out to be an omen.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1 Kings 12 Rehoboam says 'my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions'.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth zodiac sign is the scorpion, the creature Rehoboam named as his punishment.

clue.text: Oriental team in new form of show

indicators.note: a new form of the letters means they are rearranged

parts.note: Oriental means eastern, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: An Eastern sports side appears in a reworked version of a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: E (Oriental, east) plus TEAM and IN are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: An afternoon performance at a theatre or cinema is a kind of show.

clue.text: This dog in variety shows? Just the, opposite

definitions.text: This dog in variety shows? Just the, opposite

parts.words: This dog in variety shows? Just the, opposite
parts.note: this dog is not seen at variety shows; instead the variety, its mixed breeding, shows in the dog

explanation.surface: A question whether a performing dog appears on the music-hall stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-bred dog of no single breed shows a mix of varieties.

clue.text: Grounds of a sound Cambridge school

indicators.note: sound here signals a word that is said the same as the one the school's name gives

parts.note: The Leys is a well-known independent school in Cambridge

explanation.surface: A remark on the playing fields of a reputable Cambridge school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' suggests playing fields; it means the dregs in a cup or bottle. 'sound' looks like praise for the school but is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee grounds and wine dregs are both sediment left at the bottom.

clue.text: Trouble afoot for the naval chief?

parts.note: a commanding officer is CO
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A worry that some mischief is brewing for an admiral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble afoot' means a plot brewing; really it is a painful thickening on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard painful patch of skin on a toe is a common foot complaint.

clue.text: Possibly the old style of characteristic spirit

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: OS stands for Old Style, the Julian calendar dating

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a traditional manner shows a distinctive mood.
explanation.walkthrough: THE plus OS (Old Style, the dating of the Julian calendar) are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The distinctive outlook and values of a group or era make up its guiding character.

clue.text: Language of a farm-worker, one concludes

indicators.note: concludes means the one comes at the end, after the farm-worker

parts.note: a hind is an old word for a farm labourer
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A farm labourer speaks and a listener draws a conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: HIND is an old Scottish and northern English word for a skilled farm-worker.
explanation.definitionFit: The main language of northern India.

clue.text: Woodcutter does some, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the letters are said the same as another word

parts.note: read as 'does sums', which means adds

explanation.surface: A lumberjack does some work, we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does some' is heard as 'does sums', to add up figures.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool like an axe with an arched blade at right angles, for shaping timber.

clue.text: One of the nymphs Akenside hymned

definitions.meaning: a water nymph of Greek myth, presiding over springs and rivers
the 18th-century poet Mark Akenside wrote a Hymn to the water nymphs of this kind

explanation.surface: A poet sang the praises of a mythical maiden.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek myth peopled springs and streams with female spirits; Akenside's ode celebrated them.

clue.text: Fish with broken cane, maybe.

parts.note: a perch is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: broken says the letters of the word after it are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: An angler's fish might be caught with a snapped rod.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for possibly or perhaps.

clue.text: Picturesque old-characters

parts.note: not quaint elderly folk but ancient written symbols made of pictures, as in Egyptian inscriptions

explanation.surface: A description of colourful elderly eccentrics.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Egyptian writing used pictorial symbols as letters.
